title: A bad-set frequency bound
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $\varepsilon>0$, and let $\gamma$ be a point of the $n$-dimensional cube over $\mathbb F_2$. Choose $\lceil 8n/\varepsilon^2\rceil$ points independently and uniformly from that cube. The probability that $\gamma\ne0$ and the absolute empirical mean of the Walsh character indexed by $\gamma$ is at least $\varepsilon$ is at most $2\exp(-4n)$.
hypotheses_covered: $\gamma$ is any point of the $n$-dimensional cube over $\mathbb F_2$
